reasons: A malformed input file has no error handling.

terms.meaning: One box in the diagram, which here is a technology.
One link between two boxes in the diagram.
A short tag such as server or database that decides how a technology connects.
A column of the diagram, such as interface or data.
A project file that lists dependencies, such as package.json.

depends_on: Node.js built-in file and path modules

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose, usage and imports
sections.what: Explains the two ways to run the script, what it reads and where it writes. Also loads the file and path tools and the project specs.
sections.why: Gives the reader the usage in one place.
sections.watch_out: AI features only come from the spec file, never from a scan.

sections.name: LAYERS
sections.title: Five layers of the diagram
sections.what: Defines the five layers of the diagram, from interface to delivery, with the labels shown to readers.
sections.why: Groups technologies into columns so the diagram is easy to read.
sections.watch_out: Layer IDs must match the layer values in the dependency list and specs, or the boxes will not group.

sections.name: DEPS, SKIP (part 1)
sections.title: Library names mapped to stack labels
sections.what: Maps package names to a readable label, a layer and a role. For example, a web framework name becomes a labelled interface technology.
sections.why: Turns raw package names into names a reader understands.
sections.watch_out: A library not on this list does not appear on the diagram. Several names share one label, and only the first with that label is kept.

sections.name: DEPS, SKIP (part 2)
sections.title: Test tools, ignored folders and model names
sections.what: Lists the test tools, sets the folders the scan should skip, and defines a pattern that recognises AI model names in source code.
sections.why: Skipping dependency and build folders keeps the scan fast and avoids counting copied code.
sections.watch_out: The model pattern only knows the model families it lists, so newer families are missed.

sections.name: walk
sections.title: Lists project files, skipping ignored folders
sections.what: Walks through a folder and returns every file, skipping the ignored folders and stopping after seven levels deep.
sections.why: Likely reason: limits how far the scan goes.
sections.watch_out: Files deeper than seven levels are silently not scanned.

sections.name: scan
sections.title: Finds the technologies a repository uses
sections.what: Reads package, Python, Docker, compose, Vercel, workflow and database schema files, plus source files for model names. Collects each technology once.
sections.why: The diagram reflects what the repository actually uses.
sections.watch_out: A malformed package.json throws an error and stops the whole scan.

sections.name: edges
sections.title: Draws links between technologies by role
sections.what: Creates links based on each technology's role, such as server to database, interface to styling, and CI to tests. The rules run in a fixed order.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows how a request moves through the stack without manual drawing.
sections.watch_out: Links come from role rules, so an unusual stack can get odd or missing links. Check the picture after a change.

sections.name: sdkFor
sections.title: Matches an AI model to its client library
sections.what: Decides whether a client library can call a model family, based on name patterns. Also reads the command line and stops with a usage message if the arguments are missing.
sections.why: Links each model to the correct client library.
sections.watch_out: Unknown model families return no match, so they fall back to the default client chosen in the links step.

sections.name: graph
sections.title: Writes stack.json for the site
sections.what: Assembles the source, layers, technologies, links and features into one object, writes it to the project's folder, removes an old codegraph.json if present, and prints a summary.
sections.why: Likely reason: removing the old file keeps the project folder from holding two versions of the diagram.
sections.watch_out: The output path is relative to the current folder, so run the script from the repository root.

summary: Builds a stack diagram file for a project from its repository files or from a hand-written spec.
purpose: Creates stack.json, which lists the project's technologies, layers, links and AI features for the project page.
why: The header explains two modes: scan a repository's manifests, or use the hand-written spec for repositories not available locally.
how: Reads the command line, loads the spec, then either scans the repository or uses the spec nodes. Applies drops and extras, works out links from each technology's role, writes the JSON file, removes an old codegraph.json if present, and prints a summary.
inputs: A project slug, a repository folder or the --spec flag, and the data in stack-specs.mjs.
outputs: public/media/projects/slug/stack.json and a one-line summary in the console.
risks: A malformed package.json stops the whole scan. Links are rule-based, so an unusual stack can get wrong or missing links. The output path is relative, so the script must run from the repository root.
debug: Read the printed counts. Zero technologies usually means the repository path is wrong. For odd links, check the role values in the dependency list and the rules in edges.
